newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum-Bonn to avoid rate signal in 30-yr issue.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum-Bonn to avoid rate signal in 30-yr issue.

text.p: The German government will seek to avoid raising fears of an interest rate increase when it issues a 30-year bond this year, Bundesbank Deputy President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said according to the Handelsblatt newspaper.

Gaddum said that in the past, German 30-year bond issues had always come when interest rates were at a low and that a new issue -- if it is launched at an unfavourable time -- could therefore spark market expectations that the next interest rate move will be up, Handelsblatt reported in Tuesday's edition.
Gaddum made the comments in an interview with Handelsblatt. He was not directly quoted.
Bonn plans to issue a 30-year bond in mid-1997. The bond will be strippable, which means its principal and coupon can be traded separately.

Gaddum also said it would be in Germany's interest as a financial centre if all debt issued by the federal government -- that means for example debt issued by a government fund to settle the debt of the former east Germany -- were made tradeable as ordinary government debt.
That would ensure sufficient liquidity in German government debt once it has been converted to euros after the launch of European monetary union, scheduled for 1999, Gaddum said.
